minutes.headline: Zoning board granted three special permits: outdoor rental display, barn setback relief, and a house demolition and rebuild.
minutes.summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals heard three special permit applications: outdoor display of rental items at 10 Massachusetts Avenue, a dimensional variation for a barn at 115 Fairview Road, and demolition and reconstruction of a house at 396 Hollis Road. Each was moved and seconded, and the chair called a voice vote on each. The first carried a 20 foot setback condition and the third a three-bedroom condition. Long stretches of the captions are radio audio from recesses.

public_comment.topic: Applicant described wanting to put out an inflatable moonwalk and small rental items so customers can see what the store rents.
Asked whether the new house is too large for the area, whether it is a five-bedroom house, septic and water problems, and how the old house will be removed.
Asked whether the shrubbery that gives privacy between the two properties would be removed.
A resident asked about the proposed pool and its fence, and later whether the sun porch or shed had a permit.

votes.motion: Grant the special permit for outdoor display of rental items at 10 Massachusetts Avenue, on condition of no closer than 20 feet setback.
Grant the special dimensional variation of 1.46 feet for the barn at 115 Fairview Road.

Grant the special permit to voluntarily demolish the house at 396 Hollis Road without abandonment, with a finding that the new home is not substantially more detrimental, limited to three bedrooms (the 2200 square foot cap was removed).

decisions.decision: Board agreed to condition the outdoor display permit on a minimum 20 foot setback, and the applicant accepted it.
Board dropped the square footage cap from the Hollis Road motion and kept the three-bedroom condition.

what_happened.line: The board voted to grant a special permit to demolish and rebuild the house at 396 Hollis Road, limited to three bedrooms; the square footage cap was dropped.
The board granted a small dimensional variation for a barn at 115 Fairview Road on a voice vote.
The board agreed to a 20 foot minimum setback for outdoor display of rental items at 10 Massachusetts Avenue, and the applicant accepted it.
The vote on the outdoor display permit was not audible in the captions, so its outcome is not confirmed here.
Neighbors asked about house size, bedroom count, septic and water, and shrubbery privacy during the Hollis Road hearing.

why_it_matters: Permit conditions such as bedroom limits and setbacks set what can be built next to existing homes, and neighbors' concerns about septic, water and privacy are handled at this board rather than at Town Meeting.
